# Frank Tindle

> Operations executive. Thirty-one years building the teams that keep
> businesses running. Based in the London area, UK.

## Summary

Frank Tindle is an operations and technology executive with 31 years in the
video games industry, across multiple BAFTA-winning studios, currently
IT & Operations Director at Supermassive Games. Open to Operations Director,
IT Director and Head of Operations roles, and to fractional or advisory
arrangements.

## Career

- **Supermassive Games Ltd** (2010–present): IT & Operations Director. Joined at 30
  employees; the studio grew to a multi-site group peaking at 387 staff, peak turnover
  of £39.1M (FY2022), and was acquired by Nordisk Games (Egmont) in July 2022.
  Built the operations function from a standing start to a team of 16, covering IT,
  workplace support, facilities, physical and cyber security, events and
  procurement. Operating budget grew from £200K to a peak of £6M. Member of the
  Senior Leadership Team. Through the industry-wide contraction, ran the function
  down from 16 to 9 as the group went from 387 people to around 170, with service
  held at or above HDI and Gartner benchmarks throughout and every staff
  satisfaction rating in the most recent reported weeks at the top mark.
- **Criterion Software Ltd / Electronic Arts Inc** (2000–2008): Head of IT, then Head of
  Operations, then Senior Manager, IT Services. Dual responsibility to Criterion Games
  (Burnout franchise — three BAFTAs for Burnout 3: Takedown in 2005) and the RenderWare
  middleware business. Criterion was Canon-owned until EA's £40M acquisition in 2004;
  led the IT integration covering Guildford, Paris, Austin and Tokyo, 300+ employees,
  with no disruption to game releases.
- **Iguana Entertainment Ltd / Acclaim Entertainment Inc** (1995–1999): Manager, MIS
  and Operations (1995–1997), then Director of Operations (1997–1999) at Acclaim
  Studios Teesside. Built a unified email system across sites in New York, Austin,
  Utah and the UK.

## Areas of expertise

Post-acquisition integration (three acquisitions across three decades; four
corporate parents — Canon, Acclaim, EA, Egmont — spanning SME to enterprise),
scaling operations through rapid growth, org design and workforce change through
both growth and contraction, office moves and estates, business continuity,
cyber and physical security, procurement and vendor management, and applying AI
to back-office work — including an automated weekly IT service report built with
Claude and the Freshservice MCP: live ticket data, AI-drafted narrative,
human-reviewed before sending, benchmarked against HDI and Gartner.
